scope: local RV64 fetch bridge to packet decoder first-failing-halfword byte provenance for page faults

results.expected_marker: fault frontier immediately blocks younger AR
results.name: bridge_continues_after_invalid_pte_frontier
results.purpose: Continue to an instruction address owner after an invalid PTE instead of closing the fetch transaction at its fault frontier.

results.expected_marker: fault transaction emits no cache fill
results.name: bridge_fills_partial_packet_before_fault_closure
results.purpose: Write the packet cache after any successful instruction halfword instead of only after a complete non-cross-page packet.

results.name: bridge_invalid_pte_records_word_split
results.purpose: Record a four-byte word boundary instead of the exact accepted halfword frontier when the second-page PTE is invalid.

results.name: bridge_misplaces_second_halfword_lane
results.purpose: Insert the packet byte-offset-two halfword into the byte-offset-four lane, breaking independently patterned prefix provenance.

results.name: bridge_output_forgets_fault_frontier
results.purpose: Replace the registered first-failing-halfword frontier with a constant four-byte split at the bridge response interface.

results.name: bridge_releases_fault_response_without_ready
results.purpose: Release the registered response owner on valid alone instead of the valid/ready handshake, dropping a backpressured fault tuple.

results.expected_marker: raw instruction tail after F is zero
results.name: bridge_scratch_preserves_unfetched_poison
results.purpose: Preserve the preceding successful packet instead of clearing a new slow-fetch scratch register, allowing stale transaction bytes to leak into the unfetched fault suffix.

results.name: bridge_uses_live_candidate_for_fault_frontier
results.purpose: Drive the fault frontier from the continuously sampled candidate PC instead of the registered response transaction owner.

results.expected_marker: fault semantic packet next uses safe prefixes
results.name: decoder_reads_faulted_slot0_prefix
results.purpose: Read raw slot0 length bits even when the slot0 prefix response is faulted instead of using the safe compressed prefix.

results.name: decoder_slot0_checks_only_prefix
results.purpose: Use only the first halfword when assigning slot0 response, allowing a 32-bit instruction tail in the fault suffix.

results.name: decoder_slot0_sanitizes_only_prefix_fault
results.purpose: Sanitize slot0 only when its prefix faults, exposing a raw 32-bit instruction whose upper half lies in the fault suffix.

results.name: decoder_slot1_checks_only_prefix
results.purpose: Use only the first halfword when assigning slot1 response, allowing a 32-bit slot1 tail in the fault suffix.

results.name: decoder_slot1_sanitizes_only_prefix_fault
results.purpose: Sanitize slot1 only when its prefix faults, exposing raw upper halfword data when the full 32-bit range crosses the frontier.

results.name: decoder_slot1_starts_at_fixed_halfword
results.purpose: Ignore a 32-bit slot0 length and force slot1 byte-range ownership to start at the first two-byte boundary.

results.name: decoder_treats_equal_boundary_as_fault
results.purpose: Treat an instruction range ending exactly at the successful frontier as touching the second-page fault suffix.

results.name: decoder_treats_zero_frontier_as_success
results.purpose: Bypass resp1 when the successful byte frontier is zero, allowing raw bytes with no successful ownership to decode.
